answer: Every account arrives through an invitation tree, so each one traces to a sponsor who loses standing when a single upheld challenge revokes a branch, and every claim is re-checked by a reviewer with nothing to gain. A farm therefore needs an atlas of sponsors and independent auditors rather than one bought rubber stamp, which puts the bridge between identity count and real work out of reach for a glacier of cheap keys, since cost now scales with the tree and not with the number of addresses.
